The science of pharmaceutical development is essential to the process of bringing a therapeutic entity from compound discovery to treatment in humans.
Most importantly, it seeks to create dosage forms for the compound that are safely consumed by humans (and animals), are stable until ingested, release the active drug product efficiently, avoid detrimental biologic interactions, have a consistent response, and have a known and controllable safety profile.
Advances in the knowledge and uses of injectable, biotech products have added a significant complexity to the drug development process.
In comparison to small molecule drug products, biological molecules have four levels of structure considerations making the development process much more complex and challenging.
Currently, over 70% of the compounds in the bio/pharmaceutical insudstry's drug development pipeline are large biological molecules.
This is a rapidly evolving area mandating continued education for those holding entry level degrees.
Graduates will have the knowledge to design and articulate a whole team approach to the product life cycle of a candidate drug molecule from initial identification through commercial launch.

Specifically, students completing this on-line certificate program will be able to 1) Describe the design and challenges of the pharmaceutical product development process from initial concept to market as well as the roles and responsibilities of each operational group; 2) Implement cGMP regulations for pharmaceutical drug substance and drug product manufacture; and 3) Develop product development strategies to optimize the creation of novel pharmaceuticals in industrial settings.

The following 14 c ourses were tabled at the Faculty Senate meeting due to the halt of the newly proposed program titled, “Transitional Doctor of Physical Therapy (tDPT).” The courses will be modified to fit the current Doctor of Physical Therapy Program and return to the senate for approval at a later date.
TDP 601 | Health Promotion, Policy, and Models of Delivery (3 crs.) Addresses theories and research on health promotion, public policy, and health delivery models at the population, organizational and individual levels.
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to evaluate, interpret and critically ana lyze literature related to health behaviors, health education, behavior modification, patient advocacy, compliance, and disease prevention.
Pre: Post-professional tDPT student, or permission from the instructor. (Accelerated Online Program) Pre: Enrollment in tDPT program, or by permission of instructor.
TDP 602 | Research and Evidence-Based Practice in Physical Therapy (3 crs.) Prepare practicing physical therapists for evidence-based practice (EBP) and clinical research.

Topics will include principles of EBP, research methods, study design, data analysis and interpretation, and research study designs for clinical resear ch.
Upon completion of this course, participants will be able to critically analyze and apply evidence for clinical practice and research. (Accelerated Online Program) Pre: Enrollment in tDPT program, or by permission of instructor.
TDP 603 | Diagnostic Imaging for Physical Therapists (3 crs.) Prepares physical therapists to compare and contrasts medical imaging techniques including X -Ray, CT scan, MRI, and ultrasound imaging.
Radiologic anatomy, normal variants, and pathological and traumatic conditions are reviewed.
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to recognize images from various modalities, recognize normal and abnormal anatomy, make decisions on whether to refer patients for imaging, and understand the scope of physical therapy practice in relation to imaging. (Accelerated Online Program) Pre: Enrollment in tDPT program, or by permission of instructor.

Topics include analysis of common classes of pharmacological agents, and their potential effects on a physical therapy assessment and plan of care.
